Alice — thanks for the clear ask.

I've put together a concise two-page brief and two supporting files: a one-page network diagram for VPC/private deployments and a short table that maps responsibilities per deployment option. I'm attaching both; sending the suggested SIG paragraph below for your SIG response. Karthik and Marcus are looped in for the technical & legal language.

Suggested SIG paragraph (paste-ready):
"Redwood Inference offers three hosting options to meet security and compliance needs: (1) Hosted: fully managed inference in Redwood's cloud with encrypted in-flight and at-rest storage, SOC‑2 controls applied, and tenancy isolation at the application layer. Customers control data sent to the API and can configure retention and access controls via the Console. (2) Dedicated: reserved GPU capacity within Redwood's infrastructure providing tenant-level isolation and predictable throughput; customers' workloads run on isolated pools and receive expanded audit logging and per-customer operational controls. (3) Private (VPC / on‑prem): deployment of Redwood's control plane and/or runtime into a customer-managed VPC or on‑prem environment; customers retain network control, optional integration with customer KMS/HSM, and full responsibility for infrastructure-side controls while Redwood provides the platform software and operational guidance."

Data residency & KMS notes: For Hosted and Dedicated, region selection controls where compute and persistent storage are placed; Redwood supports regional pinning for EU/US workloads. For Private deployments, customers manage their own keys; Redwood supports customer-managed KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) or on‑prem HSMs as part of the deployment runbook.

Attachments: redwood_sig_hosted_vs_dedicated_table.xlsx (responsibility matrix), redwood_network_diagram_vpc.pdf (VPC / on‑prem topology).

If you want, Marcus can add a short MPA clause example for procurement to reference — Marcus, can you draft a one‑paragraph MPA blurb we can share?

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security Outreach
Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com

Following up with suggested technical snippets you can drop into the SIG fields or attach as evidence. I kept these short so procurement auditors can paste them directly.

- Tenant isolation (Dedicated): "Dedicated deployments allocate customer workloads to reserved GPU pools with per-tenant orchestration namespaces, isolated logging endpoints, and network ACLs preventing cross-tenant access. Access to customer runtime nodes is controlled through role-based access and SSH jump hosts limited to the operations team under MFA."

- Data residency: "Region pinning is supported for Hosted/Dedicated. Persistent artifacts (logs and model artifacts) are stored in the selected cloud region. For Private/VPC, storage location is customer controlled and subject to customer infrastructure settings."

- KMS: "Private deployments support integration with customer-managed keys. Redwood's runtime can be configured to use KMIP/HSM-backed keys or standard cloud KMS APIs; Redwood never stores unencrypted customer key material."

Marcus — for MPA language, I recommend a short clause about 'deployment responsibility', focusing on network control and KMS. Grace — if that reads OK I'll convert to a single-paragraph MPA example and attach.

-karthik
